messages:
leo: Seeing a flurry of RDMA connection resets for multi-GPU NCCL jobs in eu-west yesterday evening. Not obvious MTU mismatch — tests pass, but large collective ops spike packet drops on egress -> QP retry_exceeded. Posting logs.
leo: dmesg snippet:
```
mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: mlx5e: egress drop: qid 1024 cnt 1245 burst 512
ib_qp 0x3fff: QP 112345 retry_exceeded
```
leo: ethtool -S on the mlx5 shows big tx_queues stalls during bursts. ibv_devinfo OK. Running rdma pingpong doesn't repro unless I crank the send size and concurrency.
sasha: rough guess: egress shaping at ToR/tor-config causing microbursts to exceed NIC SQ capacity -> doorbell backpressure -> QP stalls. Did we push any egress qdisc changes during that deploy? @devops-oncall 
devops-oncall: not intentionally. We did enable pacing on a subset of nodes (cost work) — set tc fq_codel on igb devices. I assumed it was only host NICs, not the Mellanox ancestry. I'll pull the change set. Which nodes affected?
leo: nodes: euw-gpu-pool-3 (a,b,c) — all ML jobs on that pool failed within windows. Pattern: job ramps up tokens -> short timeouts -> killer resets. I have per-pod netstat/ss showing retransmits spike. Also NCCL logs show "transport/eth: timeout" followed by QP error.
maria: can you paste the exact rdma ping command you ran? I want to reproduce locally with similar message size/rate.
leo: ran:
```
ibv_rc_pingpong -S -s 65536 -i 0 -F 2 -N 16 <src> <dst>
# and a custom app that does 20 concurrent ibv_post_send bursts of 64KB each
```
leo: when I increase concurrency to 20+ and burst size > 256KB I see the same egress drop counters. With concurrency <=4 it's stable.
ali: interesting — Mellanox cards have SQ limits and max_burst settings. Also mlx5 driver will coalesce doorbells depending on stride; microburst could overflow NIC SQ or the ToR egress buffer. Could be exacerbated by kernel HZ and NAPI poll settings.
ali: quick triage checklist:
- check switch egress buffer/port drops with sFlow or switch counters
- run `ib_read_bw`/`ib_write_bw` with same thread counts
- try `mlxconfig -d /dev/mst/mt4099pciconf0 set STAT_RATE=0`? (just example setting)
maria: try disabling host-side pacing on a test node (tc qdisc del dev <if> root) and repro. If removing pacing removes drops, we found a conflict between host-level qdisc and NIC-level scheduling.
devops-oncall: I rolled back the recent tc change on one node and re-ran the workload — early signs: no QP error within the same ramp. Rolling back across pool now as mitigation.
leo: rolling back helps — fewer egress drop counters and jobs complete. So conflict confirmed. Need longer-term fix because removing pacing increases token cost for small jobs.
sasha: long-term options:
- move pacing to ToR shaping with awareness of RDMA (but many switches don't inspect RoCE flows well)
- limit application concurrency/burst at the NCCL/launcher layer (throttle collective start)
- tune NIC driver SQ parameters or disable host pacing only on RDMA nodes
ali: also consider enabling per-queue steering so RDMA traffic uses isolated queues and bypasses generic tc classes. For Mellanox, map flows by VLAN/DSCP to dedicated SQs if switch supports it.
maria: action items:
- ali: can you enumerate driver tunables that affect doorbell bursting and SQ depth? (priority)
- devops-oncall: we agreed to rollback across pool (in progress) and add a guard so future tc pushes exclude RDMA nodes
- leo: collect a minimal repro script and exact ethtool/ib counters for postmortem
ali: will list mlx5 tunables and quick tests. early suspects: `mlx5_core.sq_max_wqes`, `mlx5_core.hairpin_*`, and kernel NAPI polling knobs.
infra-bot: Deploy rollback completed on euw-gpu-pool-3 at 2025-08-05T19:04:25Z :white_check_mark:
leo: thanks — jobs are stabilizing. We'll follow up with a postmortem + recommended network policy change. Adding an alert: when mlx5 egress_drop > 100 in 5m, page infra oncall.
sasha: +1 to alert. Also add a config gate for tc changes that runs a quick RDMA smoke test on a canary RDMA node.
devops-oncall: noted. I'll add the canary and blocklist RDMA labels from future pacing deploys unless flagged.
leo: great. I'll upload the NCCL logs and the small repro script to the incident folder.
maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
